spec.objective: Create the new single-file, whole-file, pure/deterministic, stdlib-only Python module ngv2/dedup.py (working_dir /home/xnihil0zer0/NobleGreedv2) that provides deduplication over ngv2.contracts.Finding by exposing normalize_title, is_duplicate, and filter_new(findings, existing_titles). The module must satisfy the already-committed leaf oracle tests/test_dedup.py without authoring any new tests and without touching any other module.
functional_requirements: normalize_title(title) returns a canonical, deterministic normalized form of a finding title (e.g. case-folded, leading/trailing whitespace stripped, internal whitespace collapsed, and punctuation/formatting normalized) such that titles that differ only by these incidental variations map to the identical normalized string.

is_duplicate(...) reports whether a given finding/title is a duplicate of previously-seen titles by comparing normalized forms, returning a deterministic boolean; the exact parameter shape (e.g. (title, existing_titles) or (finding, existing_titles)) must match the call sites in the committed oracle tests/test_dedup.py.

filter_new(findings, existing_titles) returns the subset of findings whose normalized title is not present among the normalized existing_titles, preserving the input order of the surviving findings and suppressing intra-batch duplicates (the first occurrence of each newly-seen normalized title is kept).

The module operates correctly over the ngv2.contracts.Finding shape, importing Finding from ngv2.contracts, and uses only the Python standard library with no I/O, no shared mutable state, and fully deterministic behavior.
spec.interfaces: ngv2/dedup.py exposes normalize_title(...), is_duplicate(...), and filter_new(findings, existing_titles) over ngv2.contracts.Finding. working_dir: /home/xnihil0zer0/NobleGreedv2. verification_command: python -m pytest tests/test_dedup.py -q.
edge_cases: Empty title string and title that is only whitespace/punctuation normalize to a stable, well-defined value.
Titles differing only by case, surrounding/internal whitespace, or punctuation are treated as the same after normalization.
filter_new with an empty findings sequence returns an empty result; with empty existing_titles returns all findings minus intra-batch duplicates.
Two findings in the same input batch that normalize to the same title: only the first is kept by filter_new.
existing_titles supplied with non-normalized (raw) titles are still matched because both sides are normalized before comparison.
Unicode and mixed-width whitespace in titles are handled deterministically.
None or missing title handling is consistent with what the committed oracle expects (do not crash on the inputs the oracle exercises).

# COMMITTED ORACLE CONTRACT (authoritative; you cannot read these files at synthesis time so they are reproduced verbatim -- your code MUST make them pass):

## tests/test_dedup.py
```python
"""RED oracle for ngv2.dedup — drop findings whose title collides with an
existing huntr submission (saturation/dup guard). Imports ngv2.contracts.Finding."""
from ngv2.contracts import Finding
from ngv2.dedup import normalize_title, is_duplicate, filter_new


def _f(fid, title):
    return Finding(id=fid, target='berriai/litellm', category='CWE-918',
                   severity='high', title=title, description='d')


EXISTING = ['SSRF in LiteLLM proxy', 'XSS in admin UI']


def test_normalize_title_lowercases_and_collapses_ws():
    assert normalize_title('  SSRF   in   Proxy ') == 'ssrf in proxy'


def test_is_duplicate_substring_either_direction():
    # candidate is substring of an existing title (normalized)
    assert is_duplicate('ssrf in litellm proxy', EXISTING) is True
    # existing is substring of candidate
    assert is_duplicate('A new XSS in admin UI via avatar upload', EXISTING) is True
    # genuinely new
    assert is_duplicate('SQL injection in billing', EXISTING) is False


def test_filter_new_keeps_only_novel_findings():
    findings = [
        _f('1', 'SSRF in LiteLLM proxy'),       # dup
        _f('2', 'SQL injection in billing'),    # new
        _f('3', 'XSS in admin UI'),             # dup
    ]
    out = filter_new(findings, EXISTING)
    assert [f.id for f in out] == ['2']
    # returns Finding objects, input order preserved among kept
    assert all(isinstance(f, Finding) for f in out)


def test_filter_new_empty_existing_keeps_all():
    findings = [_f('1', 'anything'), _f('2', 'else')]
    assert [f.id for f in filter_new(findings, [])] == ['1', '2']


def test_filter_new_does_not_mutate_input():
    findings = [_f('1', 'SSRF in LiteLLM proxy'), _f('2', 'novel')]
    _ = filter_new(findings, EXISTING)
    assert [f.id for f in findings] == ['1', '2']

```
